South Africa Interest Rate Decisions 2026: a live SARB and ZAR tracker for Cape Town property

2026.10.12 15 min read Scott Huang Offshore Property

The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) has now held five Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meetings in 2026. January and March brought no change. On 28 May and again on 23 September the committee raised the repo rate by 25 basis points each time, taking it from 6.75% to 7.25% and prime to 10.75%, effective 25 September. Over the same period the rand traded between roughly 15.93 and 17.30 against the dollar, quoting near 16.50 on 12 October 2026. For Taiwan-based investors looking at South Africa, the policy rate, the rand and fixed-deposit rates are three faces of the same story and belong on one page.

This is a standing tracker for South Africa interest rate 2026: the SARB meeting calendar and every decision so far, the institutional range behind the rand exchange rate outlook, live South African fixed-deposit rates, and the three dates that matter before the next decision on 19 November. Every figure carries its source and the date it was checked, and yields are shown as market-reference ranges. Rates and exchange rates move; this article is information only and is not investment advice.

Key takeaway:South Africa has raised interest rates twice in 2026 (28 May and 23 September). The repo rate is 7.25% and prime is 10.75%; the next decision is 19 November, with September CPI due on 21 October. The 15-provider consensus has the rand firming to 16.21 by end-2026 and 15.92 by mid-2027. Twelve-month fixed deposits reach about 8.75% as a market-reference range.

Where do South Africa interest rate decisions stand in 2026?

Five meetings done, two hikes and three holds, and the repo rate has moved from 6.75% to 7.25%. The SARB scheduled six meetings for 2026 and has completed five. The two increases came on 28 May and 23 September, both 25 basis points and both unanimous. Because prime sits at a fixed 3.5 percentage-point spread over the repo rate, prime moved with it from 10.25% to 10.75%.

Decision dateOutcomeRepo ratePrimeEffective
29 Jan 2026No change6.75%10.25%30 Jan 2026
26 Mar 2026No change6.75%10.25%Unchanged
28 May 2026+25bp (unanimous)7.00%10.50%29 May 2026
23 Jul 2026No change (4-2 split)7.00%10.50%Unchanged
23 Sep 2026+25bp (unanimous)7.25%10.75%25 Sep 2026
19 Nov 2026Not yet heldPendingPendingPending

Zoom out and you get a complete cut, pivot and re-hike cycle. During the pandemic in 2020 the repo rate was cut to 3.50%. It rose to 8.25% through 2021 to 2023, fell back to 6.75% through 2024 and 2025, and reversed upwards again in 2026. South Africa's 2023 peak prime rate was 11.75%, so today's 10.75% still sits a full percentage point below that high, which is a useful anchor when you are judging mortgage pressure on a Cape Town purchase.

For a Taiwan buyer preparing to invest in Cape Town, the practical reading is this: local borrowing costs in South Africa have risen 50 basis points in 2026, and the SARB's own projection has the policy rate broadly stable through the rest of the year. Unless the September CPI print on 21 October goes badly wrong, the sarb repo rate 2026 line most likely stays at 7.25% until 19 November.

(Source: SARB published 2026 MPC meeting dates (29 Jan, 26 Mar, 28 May, 23 Jul, 23 Sep, 19 Nov); TradeAnswers, SARB Repo Rate History, updated 27 September 2026; MoneyZA, Best Fixed Deposit Rates South Africa, 30 September 2026.) (Source: TradeAnswers, 2026-09-27)

Why did South Africa hike while CPI was cooling?

Because the inflation was imported fuel, not domestic demand. South African CPI sat near a 2026 low of about 3.0% in February, then climbed for five consecutive months to 5.0% in June, easing to 4.3% in July and 4.4% in August. The SARB nonetheless raised rates in May and again in September, describing a large and persistent global supply shock: the Middle East conflict disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and fuel prices rose more than 34% over the twelve months to June.

MonthHeadline CPI (y/y)What was happening
Feb 2026About 3.0% (2026 low)Inflation briefly close to the SARB objective
Jun 20265.0% (2026 high)Transport inflation 12.7%; diesel +50.8% and petrol +31.7% y/y
Jul 20264.3%The fuel shock began to fade
Aug 20264.4%+0.0% month on month, below the 4.5% forecast
Sep 2026Due 21 October 2026The single most important print before the November decision

In November 2025 the SARB moved from a 3% to 6% target band to a single 3% objective, which is why a 4.4% reading that once sat comfortably inside the band now counts as clearly above target. Over the same period the US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan all tightened as well, so South Africa was not acting alone. Reading the hikes as one part of a synchronised global tightening cycle is closer to the facts than reading them as domestic overheating.

That structure matters for the Cape Town property market. If inflation is fuel-driven rather than demand-driven, rental and price fundamentals in the Western Cape have not overheated in step. The SARB itself cut its 2026 GDP growth forecast from 1.4% to 1.2% and pushed the return of inflation to near 3% out to the end of 2027, a classic mix of higher inflation and lower growth. For capital heading into South African property, the implication is that pacing the entry matters more than timing it.

(Source: Statistics South Africa consumer price index, published mid-month for the prior month; TradeAnswers, South African Inflation (CPI) History, 2026-09-27; SARB September 2026 monetary policy statement forecasts.) (Source: StatsSA via TradeAnswers, 2026-09-27)

Which way is the rand headed? The 2026 to 2027 range, unpacked

The institutional consensus leans firmer, but the range is wide. On 12 October 2026 USD/ZAR quoted near 16.50, about 3.6% above the recent low of 15.93 on 25 August 2026. A consensus of 15 providers sets the ZAR exchange rate outlook at 16.21 by end-2026, 15.92 by mid-2027 and 15.72 by end-2027, which is to say the consensus expects the rand to strengthen gradually.

PeriodUSD/ZAR consensusProvider rangeProviders bullish on ZAR
Spot (12 Oct 2026)16.50415.502 to 17.301Baseline
End 202616.20915.500 to 17.30174%
Mid 202715.91915.500 to 16.50292%
End 202715.71615.500 to 16.000100%

Why do rates drive the rand? The answer is the carry differential. At 7.25%, the South African repo rate is still high relative to major currencies, and as long as that gap holds, holding rand has an attraction. Conversely, when South Africa moves into a cutting cycle the differential narrows, which usually works against the rand. That is why the rand often reacts within seconds of an SARB announcement, while the effect of rates on inflation takes several quarters to show up.

Translated into Taiwan dollars it is easier to picture. With USD/TWD near 31.92 on 12 October 2026, one rand is worth roughly TWD 1.93. If the rand reaches the 15.72 consensus, the same Taiwan-dollar amount would buy about 5% more rand than today, which is a real difference for the deposit on a Cape Town purchase. Note, though, that the provider range runs from 15.50 to 17.30: these are forecasts, not guarantees, and the rand can move sharply on global risk sentiment.

(Source: Exchange Rates UK, USD/ZAR Forecast, 15-provider survey timestamped 12 October 2026 01:05 BST, including the provider range and bullish shares; USD/TWD spot referenced from Yahoo Finance currency quotes, 12 October 2026.) (Source: Exchange Rates UK, 2026-10-12)

What are South African fixed deposit rates right now?

The best verified 12-month rate is about 8.75%, as a market-reference range. On 30 September 2026 the highest 12-month fixed deposit rate you could verify on a bank's own website was GoTyme Bank at 8.75%, with no minimum deposit; the big four ranged from 6.60% to 8.15%. Note that South African banks quote the same product three ways, as a nominal rate, an effective rate and an amount at maturity, and the three can differ by about 0.3 percentage points.

Institution12-month rateMinimum
GoTyme Bank8.75% (simple interest)No minimum
Standard Bank7.85% nominal / 8.15% at maturity (R10,000 to R99,999)R1,000
African BankUp to 7.49% nominal (R1 million and above)Low entry
Absa7.10% nominal on R10,000R1,000
Nedbank6.60% to 7.15% nominal / 6.80% to 7.38% at maturityR1,000
RSA Retail Savings Bonds (2 / 3 / 5 years)8.00% / 8.25% / 8.75% (September 2026)R1,000

Three details people miss. First, deposit insurance under CODI has covered R100,000 per depositor per bank since 1 April 2024, and anything above that must be claimed from the liquidator, so holding R400,000 across four banks keeps all of it covered. Second, SARS exempts the first R23,800 of local interest per year for people under 65 and R34,500 from age 65. Third, a rand fixed deposit is a fixed-rate contract, so deposits already open do not change when the repo rate rises; only new deposits get the new rate.

Real returns divide rather than subtract. A nominal 8.25% deposit against 4.4% South African CPI returns about 3.69% in real terms before tax; at a 31% marginal rate the real after-tax return is roughly 1.24%. Actual returns will move with market conditions, investment carries risk including loss of capital, each bank's rate card is binding on the day you invest, and the figures above are market-reference ranges and do not constitute a promise of income.

(Source: MoneyZA, Best Fixed Deposit Rates South Africa, rates verified 30 September 2026 across GoTyme, Standard Bank, Absa, African Bank, Nedbank and RSA Retail Savings Bonds; CODI deposit insurance and SARS interest exemptions from the same source.) (Source: MoneyZA, 2026-09-30)

How do South Africa interest rate decisions hit Cape Town mortgages and buyers?

Every 25 basis points adds roughly R170 a month on a R1 million, 20-year bond. The two 2026 hikes total 50 basis points; the table below shows what that does to monthly instalments at different loan sizes, which is the most direct cash-flow change when you assess a Cape Town purchase.

Loan sizeInstalment change per 25bpOver 20 years
R750,000About +R125 a monthAbout +R30,000
R1,000,000About +R170 a monthAbout +R41,000
R1,500,000About +R250 a monthAbout +R60,000
R2,000,000About +R335 a monthAbout +R80,000

But the advertised rate is not the rate you get. ooba reported that the average South African home loan in August 2026 was priced at prime minus 0.75%, against prime minus 0.64% for January to July, so negotiability widened slightly after the hikes. South African banks also typically cap the instalment at about 30% of monthly income, which means a rate rise shrinks what the same income can borrow. For foreign buyers looking at Cape Town, that puts more weight on the size of the deposit.

Back to fundamentals. City-wide gross rental yields on Cape Town apartments sit in a market-reference range around 9.49% (the national average is about 11.53%), with net yields typically 1.5 to 2 percentage points lower, and historical annual price growth in the Western Cape sits in a market-reference range of about 4% to 7%. With the policy rate at 10.75%, the rand near 16.50 and rental yields still around 8%, the question for a Cape Town purchase shifts from whether there is capital gain to whether the cash flow covers the cost of finance.

One caveat: the yields and growth rates above are market-reference ranges, full-occupancy income depends on actual letting conditions, and past performance does not indicate future returns. How should a Taiwan investor use this tracker, and which three dates matter?

Watch three dates: 21 October, 19 November, and the inflation path through 2027. South African rates and the rand are not daily news; they run on a three to six month rhythm. Put these three markers in your calendar and you have the main line from South Africa interest rate 2026 into 2027.

1

21 October 2026: September CPI

The last key inflation print before the November decision. A reading clearly above August's 4.4% would raise the odds of another hike, which usually firms the rand and lifts expected mortgage costs in South Africa.

2

19 November 2026: the year's final SARB decision

The SARB has said its projection has the policy rate broadly stable through the rest of 2026 and most institutions expect a hold. What matters is not the headline but the vote split and the updated forecasts.

3

From 2027: does inflation return to near 3%?

The SARB expects inflation back near its 3% objective towards the end of 2027, which is where a cutting cycle would begin. If that plays out, both South African mortgage costs and the rand move into a different phase.

In practice the two decisions a Taiwan investor actually controls are the rhythm of phased currency transfers, and the split between debt and cash. With USD/ZAR near 16.50 and the consensus leaning towards a firmer rand, splitting capital into three or four tranches timed around CPI and MPC dates usually spreads currency risk better than a single large conversion. If local borrowing in South Africa is needed, confirm the borrowable amount and the achievable rate first; prime minus 0.75% is an August 2026 market reference, not a guarantee.

FAQ

Will South Africa raise interest rates again in 2026?

It depends on the oil price and the September CPI print. After its second hike on 23 September, the SARB said its projection has the policy rate broadly stable through the rest of 2026 and expects inflation back near 3% towards the end of 2027. Most institutions therefore expect a hold on 19 November; a September CPI print well above 4.4% on 21 October would raise the odds of another move. This is a market-reference scenario, not a guarantee.

Which way is the rand heading?

Most institutions lean towards a firmer rand. On 12 October 2026 USD/ZAR traded near 16.50, while the 15-provider consensus is 16.21 for end-2026, 15.92 by mid-2027 and 15.72 by end-2027, with 74% of surveyed providers bullish on the rand. The provider range is wide, from 15.50 to 17.30. These are forecasts, not guarantees, and the rand also moves around roughly TWD 1.93.

Is a South African fixed deposit worth locking up for a long term?

Check the real return first. On 30 September 2026, the best verified 12-month rate was about 8.75% (market-reference range), but August 2026 CPI was 4.4%, so a nominal 8.25% compounds to roughly 3.69% in real terms before tax. Locking up longer costs liquidity, and actual returns will move with market conditions. Confirm the bank's rate card on the day you invest.

South Africa interest rate 2026 is high - is now a good time to send money for Cape Town property?

A high policy rate is not the same as a favourable exchange rate, so keep the two apart. The policy rate sets local mortgage costs and deposit returns in South Africa; the exchange rate sets how many rand your Taiwan dollars buy. As of October 2026 the rand sits near 16.50 against the dollar with most institutions forecasting mild strength. Phasing transfers usually spreads currency risk better than one large lump sum. DingYao provides market analysis and cross-border funding-structure advisory, and does not act as a property broker or agent in Taiwan.

Which is lower risk, a rand fixed deposit or Cape Town rental income?

They are not comparable. A rand fixed deposit is a fixed-rate contract whose main risks are bank credit (deposit insurance covers R100,000 per depositor per bank) and currency. Cape Town rental income is an operating cash flow whose risks are vacancy, management fees, municipal rates and currency. City-wide gross rental yields in Cape Town sit in a market-reference range around 9.49% (the national average is about 11.53%), with net yields typically 1.5-2 percentage points lower. Past performance does not indicate future returns.

Where can I check the SARB repo rate 2026 decisions officially?

The SARB's own monetary policy and MPC announcement pages are the primary source: the statement, the vote split and the updated inflation and growth forecasts are published together on the final Thursday afternoon, South African time. Every date and figure in this tracker carries its source and the date it was checked; the formal decisions and final data remain those of the SARB and StatsSA.
